chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one who is rejected from among the witnesses, so he said: 'The suspicious (al-zannin) and the adversary (al-khasm)'. I said, 'So what about the immoral (al-fasiq) and the treacherous (al-kha'in)?' He said, 'All of this is included in the suspicious (al-zannin)'.

key_terms.الظَّنِينُ: the suspicious (one whose testimony is suspect due to minor sins or specific traits)
key_terms.الْخَائِنُ: the treacherous (one known for dishonesty or breach of trust)
key_terms.الْخَصْمُ: the adversary (one who is a party to the dispute or has a conflict of interest)
key_terms.الْفَاسِقُ: the immoral (one who commits minor sins openly)

ai.seo_question: Who are the rejected witnesses in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential criteria for witness rejection (*rad al-shuhud*) by categorizing 'the suspicious' (*al-zannin*) as an umbrella term encompassing specific defects like immorality (*fasiq*) and treachery (*kha'in*). This definition reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *'udl* (uprightness) and the nuanced evaluation of a witness's moral character (*siyagh*) beyond mere technical compliance, ensuring the integrity of testimony in legal matters.

en.hubeali: From him, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about those from the witnesses who are rejected. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The suspicious, and the adversary’. I said, ‘So (what about) the immoral and the treacherous?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is included in the suspicious’.
en.sarwar: It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the witnesses whose testimony is rejected. He (the Imam) said, ‘Of such people are a pessimist and an antagonist.’ I then asked, ‘What about a sinful and a treacherous one?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Such ones are included in “pessimist”.”’
